theater: 范迪門地東南部與黑線防區

battle.name: 黑色戰爭
battle.theater: 范迪門地東南部與黑線防區
battle.brief: 一八二六年瓦迪門地公司在德文特河谷開埠霍巴特；一八二七至一八三一年總督府沿東岸築起約三百公里黑線，以站所、鐵鏈與石牆切斷內陸。卡面野砲是十六世紀西班牙可拆件曳引的野戰砲，其可計算砲火的理念正是英軍野砲兵的骨架，但此砲未曾在塔斯馬尼亞開火，勝負由線、站所與搜索隊決定。

kit.name: 野砲
kit.history: 能拆成幾件馬車拉走的砲。它讓野戰第一次有了可以計算的砲火。

countries: 交戰的兩方，一方是英國在塔斯馬尼亞（當時稱范迪門地）的整套殖民與軍事機器。總督府由總督喬治·阿瑟主持，一八二四年至一八三六年在任，負責發出搜索令、懸賞與徵召；英軍第七十三（高地）步兵團派駐分遣隊一八二七年抵島，成為島上唯一的常備步兵；皇家工程兵分隊架橋、修路、築柵，皇家炮兵分隊攜野戰砲駐紮；瓦迪門地公司則握有全島開墾專利，以囚犯勞役開路、墾地、牧羊，囚犯編成的道路隊、牧場隊與站所守備分隊守住沿線各點。指揮分作四層：總督府定政策與賞罰，駐軍分遣隊負責成規模的搜索與接戰，公司監督與囚犯隊維護線的實體，原住民嚮導與追蹤者提供足跡、營地與水源的情報。另一方是帕拉瓦人各部族，沒有常備軍、沒有旗號、沒有成文指揮系統，以血緣與地域組成一支支武裝隊伍，主要活動在奧伊斯特灣、大河與友誼河內陸；武裝以澳洲長矛、標槍、石斧為主，火槍則來自海豹獵人與捕鯨船隊留下的滑膛前膛獵槍。他們熟悉地形、能夜間行軍、不與營級部隊正面交鋒，改以小隊襲擊孤立站所、伏擊巡邏與車隊、割斷道路、驚散牲畜。
countriesEn: The two sides were, on the one hand, the entire colonial and military apparatus of the British settlement in Van Diemen's Land, the island now called Tasmania. The governor's office, headed by Governor George Arthur, in post from 1824 to 1836, issued the search orders, the rewards and the calls for service. A detachment of the 73rd (Highland) Regiment of Foot reached the island in 1827 and became the only standing infantry on Tasmania. A company of Royal Engineers bridged streams, cut roads and built stockades; a detachment of Royal Artillery brought field guns with it; and the Van Diemen's Land Company, holding the sole right to colonise the island, opened roads, cleared land and ran sheep with convict labour, while convicts organised into road gangs, stock gangs and outstation guards held the line at every post along it. Command ran in four layers: the governor's office set policy and penalties, the stationed detachment fought the pitched actions, company overseers and convict gangs maintained the physical line, and Aboriginal guides and trackers supplied information on tracks, camps and water. The other side was the Palawa people, organised by kinship and country into armed bands with no standing army, no banners and no written chain of command, whose main ground was the interior around Oyster Bay, the Big River and the Friendly River. Their weapons were Australian spears, throwing spears and stone axes, with a handful of smooth-bore muzzle-loading hunting guns that had come to the island with the sealers and whalers. They knew the country, could move by night, avoided pitched action against battalion-sized columns, and worked instead in small parties: raiding isolated outstations, ambushing patrols and supply convoys, cutting the roads and driving off the flocks.
people: 關鍵人物橫跨兩套權力結構。英方以總督喬治·阿瑟為核心，他既要向倫敦交代殖民開墾的進度，又要維持島上秩序，於一八二七年批准把「黑線」列為政府工程；瓦迪門地公司駐地總監約翰·佩德是施工與勞役的實際主持者，其嚴厲管治在殖民地檔案與後世研究中屢被提及。軍方則由第七十三團派駐分遣隊的軍官、皇家炮兵分隊的砲長與工程兵分隊的指揮官分頭負責搜索、築線與通信。原住民一方沒有職銜，只能從殖民地法庭紀錄與後世口述史中還原其名字：以綽號「蚊」與「黑比爾」記錄的隊伍首領，據當時的殖民地司法紀錄，黑比爾於一八二七年被處決；塔雷諾雷勒是有記錄的最後一位純血塔斯馬尼亞人之一，一八三〇年代在奧伊斯特灣一帶去世。追蹤者隊伍裡還有被迫或受僱為英方帶路的帕拉瓦人，他們熟悉全島道路網，是搜索隊最依賴的情報來源。一八三四年，總督府改弦更張，任命前軍官喬治·奧古斯都·羅賓遜主持調停會議，以停火與遷徙取代搜索，開啟黑線之後的另一條路。
peopleEn: The decisive figures belong to two different structures of power. On the British side the centre was Governor George Arthur, who had to answer to London for the pace of colonisation while keeping order on the island, and who in 1827 approved the Black Line as a government work. John Pedder, the chief overseer of the Van Diemen's Land Company, actually directed the works and the convict labour, and his severe regime is repeatedly mentioned in the colonial files and in later scholarship. The military side was divided among the officers of the 73rd's detachment, the gun detachment of Royal Artillery and the officer commanding the sappers of Royal Engineers, who between them ran the searching, the building and the signalling. The Aboriginal side held no offices and can be recovered only from the colony's court records and later oral history: commanders remembered by the nicknames Mosquito and Black Bill, the latter of whom was executed in 1827 according to the colonial justice records of the time; and Tarenorerer, one of the last recorded full-blood Tasmanians, who died around Oyster Bay in the 1830s. Among the trackers were Palawa men who, forced or hired, guided the British columns; they knew the island's road network better than anyone and were the chief source of information for the searches. In 1834 the government changed course and appointed the former officer George Augustus Robinson to preside over conciliatory conferences, substituting truce and removal for the search, and opening the road that followed the Black Line.
kits: 卡面那門野砲是十六世紀西班牙的野戰砲：青銅或鑄鐵炮身，重量在數百公斤之間，口徑約二至四磅，可以拆成三、四件分載，由單匹或雙匹馬拉著走，隨砲附備件箱、火藥壺與彈藥箱。它的重要性不在口徑，而在「砲火可以計算」——射程、射速、彈著事先算得出，野戰第一次有了可以編入計畫的火力。一八二六年的塔斯馬尼亞沒有這門砲；但英軍野砲兵用的正是同一概念：一門前裝滑膛鑄鐵野戰砲，旅團級六磅砲為主、支援級九磅砲為輔，配隨砲馬車、備件架、彈藥箱、火藥壺與點火工具，引信用管式引信，步兵則是滑膛燧發步槍加刺刀。炮兵在本役的位置極其樸素：不是攻城，而是用炮口焰和鳴炮在林緣製造聲音與火光，宣告站所存在、封鎖路口、驅散突擊，並在夜間對樹林方向發射實彈或空包。英方也曾試用火箭一類的新式投射武器，紀錄顯示成效有限。原住民一方的裝備更為簡陋：澳洲長矛、標槍、石斧、擲標槍，加上從海獵船隊得來的前膛獵槍，口徑約半英寸上下，數量有限且難以補充。真正決定本役的裝備其實是線的實體：削尖木柵、鐵刺、鐵鏈與石牆，以及道路隊的斧鋤、供給車隊、牛群和武器庫。卡面野砲在此的真正位置，是本役「以線代戰」這種思路的技術祖型，而非現場的火力。
kitsEn: The field gun on this card is a sixteenth-century Spanish piece: a bronze or cast-iron barrel of several hundred kilograms and about two to four pounds, broken down into three or four loads and drawn by one or two horses, with its spare-parts box, powder flask and ammunition box carried with it. Its importance lay not in calibre but in the idea that gunnery could be calculated: range, rate of fire and effect known in advance, so that firepower could for the first time be written into a plan of battle. No such gun stood in Tasmania in 1826, but British field artillery used exactly the same idea: a muzzle-loading smoothbore cast-iron field gun, with the six-pounder as the brigade piece and the nine-pounder in support, travelling on a limber with a spare-carriage rack, ammunition boxes, powder flasks and priming implements, fired by tube primer, and supported by infantry carrying smoothbore flintlock muskets and bayonets. The artillery role in this campaign was plain and unglamorous: not siege work, but the muzzle flash and the report used on the edge of the bush to make sound and light, to announce the presence of a post, to seal a path, to break up a rush, and by night to fire live or blank rounds into the treeline. The British also tried rocket weapons of the newer type, and the records show little result. The Aboriginal armament was far plainer: Australian spears, throwing spears, stone axes, and front-loading hunting guns of about half an inch calibre obtained from the sealing crews, few in number and hard to replace. The equipment that really decided the campaign was the physical line itself: sharpened stockades, iron rails, chains and stone walls, together with the axes and picks of the road gangs, the supply convoys, the flocks and the magazines. The true place of the card's field gun here is as the technological ancestor of this war of line and enclosure, not as any weapon present on the field.
tactics: 黑線不是一道圍牆，而是一套由站所、柵欄、鐵鏈、石牆與巡邏道組成的可控邊界，把島內陸分割成可以逐段搜索的扇形。站所之間保持可互相支援的距離，每所配守備、武器、馬匹與糧食，通訊靠夜間火堆信號與傳令兵。搜索由騎兵搜索隊執行：從站所出發，帶原住民嚮導，分成小組晝夜不停地沿線巡查，目標不是殲滅，而是迫使游擊隊放棄藏身之地、失去補給，最後被擠出定居區。原住民隊伍的戰術與之相反：多在夜間接近，逼近站所時以喊聲與火把製造混亂，奪取火槍、馬匹與火藥，砍倒柵欄、割斷道路、驚散羊群，隨即分散退回內陸，避免正面交鋒，英軍搜索隊若追得急，往往在熟悉地形的追蹤中反被消耗。英方的應對是分進合擊：數個站所同時出動，把搜索面疊加，並把牛羊移入線內，切斷游擊隊的獵場與水源，逼其靠近。季節直接影響節奏：南半球夏季炎熱乾旱，林間可通行，搜索最有效；秋冬多雨泥濘，車隊與砲車行動受限，衝突密度下降。炮兵在此從不主導攻勢，它的用法是聲音與火光：鳴炮宣示存在、以火光照明林緣、封鎖通道，讓地面搜索隊在視線與士氣上佔到便宜。
tacticsEn: The Black Line was not a rampart but a controllable frontier built of posts, stockades, chains, stone walls and patrol tracks, dividing the island's interior into sectors that could be searched in turn. Posts were spaced so that each could support the next, each holding a garrison, weapons, horses and stores, and communication ran on night signal fires and mounted messengers. The searching was done by mounted parties leaving the posts with Aboriginal guides, split into small groups and riding the line day and night; the object was not to destroy the bands but to drive them from their refuges, cut them off from supplies and finally squeeze them out of the settled districts. Aboriginal tactics were the mirror image: approach at night, create confusion at the post with shouting and torches, take muskets, horses and powder, cut down the stockades and the roads, scatter the sheep, then break up and withdraw into the interior, avoiding a general engagement and wearing down any patrol that pushed too hard in country they knew. The British answer was to search from several posts at once, to overlap their areas, to move the flocks inside the line and to cut the bands off from their hunting grounds and water so that they were forced toward the settlements. The seasons set the rhythm: the southern summer was hot and dry with the bush passable and the searching at its most effective, while the wet winter months turned the tracks to mud, checked the guns and the wagons and thinned out the clashes. Artillery never led an attack; its use was sound and light, the report announcing presence, flame lighting the edge of the bush, guns sealing a path, giving the searching infantry the advantage of sight and confidence.
data: 可用的數字並不多，而且多數有爭議。黑線自一八二六年底起分數段興建，至一八三一年前後完成，全長約三百公里（約一百九十英里），沿線站所約四十座，各說在三十九至四十二座之間；部分路段為削尖木柵與鐵刺網，個別路段改以鐵鏈連接立柱，另有以石塊砌成的矮牆。瓦迪門地公司一八二四年在倫敦成立，一八二五年首批船隊抵埠，取得全島開墾專利，名下約二十五萬英畝土地，其中一部分劃作囚犯配給，按當時的殖民地制度，公司分得土地收益的四成。人口方面，一八二〇年代中期島上囚犯以萬計，佔殖民地總人口大半，英國當局把范迪門地定位為流放地。原住民人口最難核實：一八二六年前後的估計由數千至逾萬不等，諸說並存，學界至今未有定論；到一八三〇年代中期，島上殘存者不足數百人，記錄同樣殘缺。軍力方面，一八二七年抵達的第七十三團分遣隊是島上唯一常備步兵，另有工程兵與炮兵各一小型分隊；英軍野砲主力為六磅砲與九磅砲，射程與威力都遠超卡面那門約二至四磅的十六世紀野砲。道路網方面，一八三一年開通的塔納小道把霍巴特與黑線東段直接連起，來回一趟需數日；霍巴特至奧伊斯特灣約五十公里。
dataEn: Few figures survive, and most of them are disputed. The Black Line was built in sections from the end of 1826 and was substantially complete by about 1831, running for roughly three hundred kilometres, about one hundred and ninety miles, with some forty posts along it by most counts, others giving thirty-nine to forty-two. Some sections were faced with sharpened stockades and iron rails; a few were marked by iron chains strung between posts, and others by low dry-stone walls. The Van Diemen's Land Company was formed in London in 1824, its first ships reached the island in 1825, and it was granted the sole right to colonise Tasmania, with about two hundred and fifty thousand acres of land in hand, part of which was allotted to convicts, and with the company taking four tenths of the land revenue under the colonial settlement. On population: through the middle of the eighteen-twenties the convicts on the island numbered in the tens of thousands and formed the majority of the colony's population, Britain having made Van Diemen's Land a penal destination. The Aboriginal population is the hardest to establish: estimates for around 1826 run from several thousand to more than ten thousand, and they differ sharply among sources, with no agreed figure to this day; by the middle of the eighteen-thirties fewer than a few hundred remained, and the records of them are fragmentary. On forces: the detachment of the 73rd that arrived in 1827 was the only standing infantry on the island, with small detachments of engineers and artillery. The British field guns were the six-pounder and the nine-pounder, outranging and outgunning the card's two- to four-pound sixteenth-century piece by a long way. On roads: Tarner's Track, opened in 1831, linked Hobart directly with the eastern end of the line, a journey of several days each way, and Hobart lay some fifty kilometres from Oyster Bay.
cause: 開戰的根源是土地。一八二四年瓦迪門地公司取得全島開墾專利，一八二五年船隊與囚犯抵島，一八二六年在德文特河谷開埠霍巴特，公司隨即在東岸牧羊、伐木、開路，把殖民線推入原住民世代使用的獵場、淡水水源與燧石產地。施工用的是囚犯勞役：道路隊清理林地，牧場隊放牧，站所與柵欄一段段往內陸推進，這套體制本身就是對原住民的壓力來源。衝突在一八二六年之後升級，奧伊斯特灣、大河一帶的武裝隊伍開始襲擊站所、襲擊警衛與監督、奪取火槍與馬匹、割斷道路並驚散羊群。英方初期反應是懲罰性搜索：懸賞、追捕、吊刑，並把小隊襲擊視為個別案件處理。這樣的處理無法消滅游擊，只把更多部族推向內陸聯合，也令每一次搜索都變成更強的報復循環。正是在這樣的背景下，總督府放棄「追到哪裡算哪裡」的辦法，轉而用一條可以丈量的線把定居區與內陸硬性分開：黑線因此不是防禦工事，而是一項用國家力量執行的鎮壓工程。它的思路也承自英帝國在印度、美洲與澳洲各地的定居邊界政策。
causeEn: The root of the war was land. In 1824 the Van Diemen's Land Company was granted the sole right to colonise the island; in 1825 its ships and convicts arrived; in 1826 it opened Hobart Town on the Derwent River, and immediately began running sheep, cutting timber and opening roads on the east coast, pushing the settled line into the hunting grounds, water sources and flint deposits the Aboriginal people had used for generations. The works were done with convict labour: road gangs cleared the bush, stock gangs grazed the flocks, posts and stockades advanced by stages into the interior, and the system itself was a source of pressure on the people it displaced. From 1826 the conflict escalated, and armed bands around Oyster Bay and the Big River began raiding outstations, attacking guards and overseers, taking muskets and horses, cutting the roads and scattering the flocks. The British answer at first was punitive search: rewards, arrests, hangings, and the treatment of each raid as a separate crime. That could not end a guerrilla war; it pushed more groups into the interior and turned every search into a cycle of revenge. In that setting the governor's office abandoned the idea of chasing the bands wherever they went and substituted a measurable line dividing the settled country from the interior. The Black Line was therefore not a fortification but a suppression work carried out by the state, and the thinking behind it was inherited from the settlement-frontier policies the British empire had pursued in India, the Americas and Australia.
impact: 黑線最直接的效果是壓縮，而它的長期代價則改寫了一整片大陸的歷史。就軍事而言，這場衝突沒有會戰，沒有勝負可判，結果由線的長度、站所的密度、馬匹的數量與道路的通行能力決定；這套「以線代戰」的做法此後被澳洲其他殖民地一再模仿，成為十九世紀末防線政策的樣板。就法制與行政而言，站所管轄、賞金制度、對土地的強制徵用與囚犯勞役的合法化，令殖民地司法長期適用於原住民群體。就社會而言，土地被奪、聚落被拆散、幾個語群相繼消失，語言與口述歷史大量失傳。就記憶而言，一八七七年最後一位已知純血塔斯馬尼亞女性去世之後，「黑色戰爭」一詞在二十世紀被重新挪用：一九七〇年代起的原住民權利運動把黑線視為核心證據，二〇一七年聯邦議會就是否承認「種族滅絕」進行辯論，至今官方道歉與否仍有分歧。對砲兵史而言，本役亦提供一個反向的提醒：野砲真正的價值不在射程，而在它能把火力算成可以隨車攜帶、隨路延伸的支援——而黑線的做法，是把這個可攜帶的火力換成一條可攜帶的界線。
impactEn: The immediate effect of the Black Line was to compress; its long-term cost rewrote the history of a continent. Militarily, this conflict produced no battle and no verdict: the result was settled by the length of the line, the density of the posts, the number of horses and the passability of the roads, and that method of substituting a line for a battle was copied repeatedly by the other Australian colonies, becoming the model for frontier-defence policy at the end of the nineteenth century. In law and administration, the jurisdiction of the posts, the reward system, the compulsory taking of land and the legalisation of convict labour extended colonial justice to Aboriginal people for decades. In society, land was taken, communities were broken up, one language group after another disappeared, and much oral history and speech was lost to the record. In memory, after the death of the last known full-blood Tasmanian woman in 1877, the phrase Black War was reclaimed in the twentieth century: Aboriginal rights campaigns from the nineteen-seventies made the Black Line their central piece of evidence, and in 2017 the federal parliament debated whether the removal should be acknowledged as genocide, a question on which official apology remains contested. For the history of artillery the campaign offers a reverse lesson: the value of a field gun lay not in its range but in turning firepower into a support that could be carried and extended along a road, and the Black Line replaced that portable firepower with a portable frontier.

resultEn: Between 1826 and 1831 the Black Line was built in sections and put into operation, some forty posts over about three hundred kilometres; Tarner's Track opened in 1831, the logistics line took shape, and the main body of resistance fell apart in the years that followed, the remaining bands withdrawing into the western highlands. In 1834 the government adopted the conciliatory conferences presided over by Robinson, exchanging truce, rations and removal for the laying down of arms, and in 1835 the remaining people were removed to Flinders Island, where the Wybalenna mission became their last settlement; large search operations continued through 1836 and 1837, and the casualty and death figures for them contradict one another in the sources and cannot be verified. By the middle of the eighteen-forties the Aboriginal population of the island was all but gone, and in 1877 the last known full-blood Tasmanian woman died, leaving the Black Line as ruin rather than frontier. Its surviving stockades and post sites were marked through the twentieth century and are today heritage places with interpretation panels. For this card the outcome can be put in one line: the calculable gunnery typified by the sixteenth-century Spanish field gun was only an ancestor in idea, and never appeared on the field; what actually won this war was a Black Line built from stockades, chains, stone walls, convict axes, post horses and the feet of trackers.
